Penn State is test-optional for first-year applicants through the fall 2025 semester, meaning standardized test scores are not required for admission.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Telecommunications

Requirements: Entrance to the Theatre major requires a successful audition or interview for all students. This is in addition to the University’s application for admission. To be eligible for entrance to the Theatre major, a student must have completed at least 18 scholarship credits at Penn State and earned at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Theatre

Requirements: Admission to the Bachelor of Fine Arts (BFA) in Theatre program at Penn State is by interview or audition. This is in addition to the standard Penn State undergraduate application. Applicants must first apply for admission to Penn State through MyPennState or the Common App and then complete a secondary artistic review process via the School of Theatre, which includes submitting a portfolio, resume, personal statement, and participating in an audition or interview depending on the specific concentration (Acting, Musical Theatre, Design and Technology, or Stage Management).
Program name: Bachelor of Fine Arts in Theatre

Requirements: For the Bachelor of Science degree in Turfgrass Science, a minimum of 120 credits is required. In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must: 1. attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average. 2. completed and earned a grade of C or better in: BIOL 110, CHEM 110, TURF 235.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Turfgrass Science

Requirements: The Bachelor of Science degree in Veterinary and Biomedical Sciences (VBSC) provides students with a strong foundation in the biological and physical sciences. For the B.S. degree in Veterinary and Biomedical Sciences, a minimum of 124 credits is required. To be eligible for entrance to the major, a student must have attained at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average. Additionally, each student must earn at least a grade of C in each of the following courses: BIOL 110, BIOL 220W, BIOL 230W, VBSC 50, VBSC 211, and MICRB 201. General first-year application requirements for Penn State include a high school diploma or equivalent and the following high school units: 4 English, 3 Mathematics, 3 Science, 3 Social Studies, and 2 World Language.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Veterinary and Biomedical Sciences

Requirements: For the Bachelor of Arts in Visual Arts, students must apply to the University and also submit a portfolio through the School of Visual Arts Slideroom. Portfolios are reviewed once a year for admission to the program in the following fall semester. To be eligible for entrance to the Visual Arts major (B.A.), a student must: 1) have completed at least 29.1 credits; 2) have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00; 3) have completed ART 1, ART 20, ART 30, ART 40, ART 50, and ARTH 111 or ARTH 112 with a grade of C or better.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Visual Arts

Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, a student must satisfy the following requirements: 1. have completed 29-59 cumulative credits; 2. have a minimum cumulative grade-point average of 2.00. For first-year students, admission is based on high school records and optional standardized test scores. Students must have a minimum of 15 units in required subject areas: 4 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics, 3 units of Science, 3 units of Social Studies, and 2 units of World Language.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in Wildlife and Fisheries Science

Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Women's Studies major, students must be enrolled in the College of the Liberal Arts or the Division of Undergraduate Studies and have a cumulative grade-point average of 2.00 or higher.
Program name: Bachelor of Arts in Women's Studies

Requirements: In order to be eligible for entrance to this major, students must satisfy the following requirements: achieve a minimum cumulative grade point average of 3.00; complete at least 48 degree-applicable credits; complete the following courses with a grade of C or better: ENGL 15 or ENGL 30, 3 credits of literature (GH) from the University-approved list, EDPSY 14 or PSYCH 100, and 6 credits of quantification (GQ); provide documentation of at least 40 hours of volunteer or paid experience with learners of the age group the candidate plans to teach; complete a speech-and-hearing screening (at no cost to the student); complete an interview with a World Languages Education faculty member; and complete a dispositional assessment.
Program name: Bachelor of Science in World Languages Education

Requirements: To apply for the Associate in Science in Business Administration, you must have a high school diploma or its equivalent (GED). High school students may apply for admission; however, they may not begin their studies until they have graduated from high school. Transfer students may also apply; however, any credit earned at another institution will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis.
Program name: Associate in Science in Business Administration

Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the Associate in Science in Criminal Justice degree program, a student must be a high school graduate or have earned a General Education Development (GED) certificate or its equivalent.
Program name: Associate in Science in Criminal Justice

Requirements: Applicants must submit a completed application, including the Self-Reported Academic Record (SRAR) or official high school transcripts. Penn State is test-optional for undergraduate admission; students may choose whether or not to include SAT or ACT scores as part of their application.
Program name: Associate in Arts in Letters, Arts, and Sciences

Requirements: For the Associate in Science degree in Human Development and Family Studies, a minimum of 60 credits is required. To be eligible for entrance to the Human Development and Family Studies major, a student must: 1) attain at least a 2.00 cumulative grade point average.
Program name: Associate in Science in Human Development and Family Studies

Requirements: Admission to the Information Sciences and Technology (ISTAS_AS) major is based on the admission requirements for Penn State. Students who meet the University's minimum requirements for admission are eligible to enroll in this major.
Program name: Associate in Science in Information Sciences and Technology

Requirements: To be eligible for admission to an associate degree, an applicant must have a high school diploma or a General Education Development (GED) credential. For the Associate in Science degree in Labor and Human Resources, a minimum of 60 credits is required.
Program name: Associate in Science in Labor and Human Resources

Requirements: Admission to the program is through the Penn State Undergraduate Admissions Office. To be considered for admission, you must have high school units in: English (4), Social Studies/Arts/Humanities (3), Science (3), Math (3, including algebra). You must have also completed one unit of high school biology and one unit of high school chemistry.
Program name: Associate in Science in Nursing

Requirements: General admission criteria are used to assess students' eligibility for the OTA program. High school grades in units of study are used to determine eligibility for admission. Prospective students must also complete 15 hours of observation in at least two different occupational therapy settings and submit a completed Clinical Observation Form with the application.
Program name: Associate in Science in Occupational Therapy Assistant

Requirements: Entry to the PTA program is a two-step process: (1) Entry to Penn State; (2) Entry to the Physical Therapist Assistant (PTA) Program. Students must first be admitted to Penn State. Once admitted, students will then apply for entry to the PTA program. Entry into the program is based on: 1) High school grades or college grades (if 18 or more college-level credits are completed); 2) SAT or ACT scores (if applicable); 3) Documentation of observation in a physical therapy setting; 4) A program application.
Program name: Associate in Science in Physical Therapist Assistant

Requirements: Admission to the program is based on high school record (GPA) or, for transfer students, college academic record. Enrollment in the Radiologic Sciences program is limited, and students must be aware that admission to the University does not guarantee admission to the clinical component of the program. Admission to the clinical component is a separate process.
Program name: Associate in Science in Radiologic Sciences

Requirements: Entrance to the Biomedical Engineering Technology major (2ET) requires that the student has: 1) completed MATH 22 or is eligible for MATH 26 or higher, and 2) completed CHEM 110. For the Associate in Engineering Technology degree in Biomedical Engineering Technology, a minimum of 68 credits is required.
Program name: Associate in Engineering Technology in Biomedical Engineering Technology

Requirements: Penn State identifies and reviews a number of factors when making an admission decision. These include your high school grades and curriculum, your standardized test scores (optional), your class rank (if available), and other factors like your application essay and involvement in activities.
Program name: Associate in Engineering Technology in Electrical Engineering Technology

Requirements: Students must have a high school diploma or its equivalent. High school unit requirements include: 3 units of English, 3 units of Mathematics (including algebra, geometry, and trigonometry), 3 units of Science, and 5 units of other subjects. This program is currently only available at the Penn State Berks and Penn State DuBois campuses. Standardized test scores (SAT or ACT) are not required for students applying for admission through the Fall 2025 semester.
Program name: Associate in Engineering Technology in Mechanical Engineering Technology

Requirements: For admission to the University, an applicant must have a high school diploma or its equivalent. To be eligible for admission to the Nanotechnology major, students must have a grade-point average of 2.0 or higher.
Program name: Associate in Engineering Technology in Nanotechnology

Requirements: There are no additional entrance requirements for this major.
Program name: Associate in Science in Wildlife Technology

Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be in a major that is not Accounting and have a cumulative grade-point average of 2.0 or higher. Admission into the Accounting minor is competitive. Students must have completed the following courses with a grade of C or better: ACCTG 211, ECON 102, and (MATH 110 or MATH 140).
Program name: Minor in Accounting

Requirements: For admission to the minor, students must have completed at least 45 credits and be in good academic standing.
Program name: Minor in Addictions and Recovery

Requirements: Any student enrolled in a major at Penn State may apply for the Aerospace Engineering minor. Some prerequisites may be required. To be admitted to the minor, students must have a grade of C or better in AERSP 311 and AERSP 313. Some courses may require prerequisites. Students may apply for admission to the minor through the LionPATH 'Update Academics' tool.
Program name: Minor in Aerospace Engineering

Requirements: A student must be at least a fifth-semester standing to apply for a minor in the College of the Liberal Arts. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. The minor requires a minimum of 18 credits.
Program name: Minor in African American Studies

Requirements: For a minor in African Studies, a minimum of 18 credits is required. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least 6 credits must be at the 400 level. To be admitted to the minor, students must have completed at least one African Studies course.
Program name: Minor in African Studies

Requirements: At least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average and at least third-semester classification are required for admission. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the supplement 400-level courses must be taken from the Department of Agricultural Economics, Sociology, and Education.
Program name: Minor in Agribusiness Management

Requirements: Admission to the minor is by permission of the minor adviser. Students are required to have a 2.00 or higher grade point average to be admitted to the minor.
Program name: Minor in Agronomy

Requirements: A student must have at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average to be accepted into a minor. A student may not declare a minor until they have attained at least third-semester classification (29.1 credits). A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. To graduate with this minor, at least 6 credits of the 18 credits for the minor must be at the 400-level.
Program name: Minor in American Studies

Requirements: To be eligible to declare a minor, a student must have completed at least 1 semester of University enrollment and be in good academic standing (2.00 or higher cumulative GPA).
Program name: Minor in Animal Science

Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major program.
Program name: Minor in Anthropology

Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, a student must have at least a 2.0 GPA. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from any other degree or minor.
Program name: Minor in Arabic

Requirements: To be admitted to a minor, an undergraduate student must be enrolled in a major and must have completed at least 18 credits at Penn State or have transferred at least 18 credits to Penn State.
Program name: Minor in Architectural History

Requirements: The minor is open to all students, except those in the pre-architecture and architecture majors. Entry into the minor requires a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or better. A student enrolled in this minor must receive a grade of C or better in all courses required for the minor, as specified in 12.A of the Senate Rules and Regulations. At least 6 credits of the minor must be unique from any other degree or minor program in which the student is enrolled.
Program name: Minor in Architecture

Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be at least 3rd-semester standing and have a 2.00 or higher cumulative grade point average.
Program name: Minor in Art

Requirements: At least six (6) credits of the minor must be unique from the 400-level courses required for the student's major program, or any other minor. To graduate with the minor, students must complete the requirements as specified by the program. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. A student may not declare a minor until they have been accepted into a major. Application for a minor is made in LionPATH.
Program name: Minor in Art History

Requirements: Students may apply for admission to the minor after they have achieved at least third-semester classification (29.1 credits).
Program name: Minor in Asian Studies

Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, a student must have at least a 2.00 cumulative GPA and have completed MATH 140 and MATH 141 with a grade of C or better. At least 18 credits are required for the minor. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the student's major degree requirements.
Program name: Minor in Astronomy and Astrophysics

Requirements: To be eligible for the Minor in Astrobiology, a student must be enrolled in a baccalaureate degree program. Requirements for a minor must be completed in conjunction with a major degree program. A student must complete at least six credits of the minor at the 400-level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by University Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from any other degree or minor earned by the student.
Program name: Minor in Astrobiology

Requirements: Students must be in at least their third semester at Penn State and have a cumulative grade-point average of 2.0 or higher. Some minors have additional requirements; however, this minor does not.
Program name: Minor in Bioethics

Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must have completed BIOL 110 and have a 2.00 or higher GPA. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major and at least six credits must be upper-level (400-level) courses.
Program name: Minor in Biology

Requirements: To be eligible for admission to the minor, a student must be enrolled in a major outside of the Smeal College of Business and have a cumulative GPA of 2.00 or higher.
Program name: Minor in Business

Requirements: To be eligible for the minor, students must have completed BLAW 341 with a grade of C or better and have a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher.
Program name: Minor in Business Law

Requirements: Students may apply for the minor in the Eberly College of Science after they have earned at least 45 credits and have been admitted to a major. Students must apply for the minor no later than the end of the second week of the semester in which they plan to graduate. For the minor in Chemistry, a minimum of 18 credits are required. At least six credits of the 18-20 credits for the minor must be at the 400-level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least 6 credits for the minor must be unique from the course requirements for a student’s major.
Program name: Minor in Chemistry

Requirements: For the minor in Chinese, a minimum of 18 credits is required. At least 6 credits must be at the 400 level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. Some courses may require prerequisites.
Program name: Minor in Chinese

Requirements: To enter the minor, students must have a 2.00 GPA and should submit an application. In the application, students state their goals for the minor and propose a series of courses and a public scholarship project to meet those goals.
Program name: Minor in Civic and Community Engagement

Requirements: Students may apply for admission to the minor after they have completed at least 3 credits of CAMS courses. To apply, students must have a minimum 2.00 grade-point average. A range of 18-24 credits is required for the minor. At least 6 credits must be at the 400-level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from any other degree or minor the student is pursuing.
Program name: Minor in Classics and Ancient Mediterranean Studies

Requirements: Admission to the minor is through the Liberal Arts Undergraduate Studies Office. A student's enrollment in the minor is normally done through LionPATH. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the 400-level courses must be taken at Penn State.
Program name: Minor in Communication Arts and Sciences

Requirements: Students with at least third-semester standing (min 29.1 credits) may be admitted to the minor by submitting an application in LionPATH. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from any other degree or minor. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Program name: Minor in Communication Sciences and Disorders

Requirements: At the start of their junior year, students can declare their minor in LionPATH. To be eligible to declare a minor, a student must be enrolled in a major and have completed at least 30 credits. A student who wishes to declare the minor in Comparative Literature should consult with the Director of Undergraduate Studies in the Department of Comparative Literature and must submit an application for the minor in LionPATH. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. To be eligible for the minor, a student must have a minimum overall grade point average of 2.00 in the courses required for the minor.
Program name: Minor in Comparative Literature

Requirements: To enter the minor, students must have completed CMPSC 121 or CMPSC 131 with a grade of C or better. A student must be in a major which does not require Computer Science (CMPSC) or Computer Engineering (CMPEN) for graduation.
Program name: Minor in Computer Science

Requirements: At least 4th semester standing is required. To be admitted, students must have a grade of C or better in ENTR 310.
Program name: Minor in Corporate Innovation and Entrepreneurship

Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. For a minor in Creative Writing, a minimum of 18 credits is required.
Program name: Minor in Creative Writing

Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, a student must have completed CRIM 100 with a grade of C or better and have at least a 2.00 cumulative grade-point average.
Program name: Minor in Criminology

Requirements: Students must have completed 29.1 credits and be enrolled in a Penn State major to apply for this minor. A student may apply for the minor in LionPATH. For more information, please contact the IST Office of Undergraduate Academic Advising. To graduate with a minor, students must satisfy the requirements for the minor, including at least 6 credits at the 400 level. In addition, a student must complete at least six credits of the minor in courses that are not being used to satisfy the requirements of the student’s major. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10.
Program name: Minor in Cybersecurity Analytics and Operations

Requirements: Students are eligible to apply for the dance minor after they have completed 6 credits in dance from the following: DANCE 170, DANCE 231, DANCE 241, DANCE 251, DANCE 261. An audition is required for entry into the minor. For a minor in Dance, a minimum of 18 credits is required. At least 6 credits must be at the 400-level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10.
Program name: Minor in Dance

Requirements: Students must apply for entrance to the minor no later than the beginning of their junior year. To apply, students must have completed ART 110S or GD 100 with a grade of C or better. Applications are submitted through the Digital Arts Minor faculty committee. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least six credits must be at the 400-level.
Program name: Minor in Digital Arts

Requirements: At least 6 credits of the minor must be separate from any other certificate, major, or minor and the student must have at least a 2.00 grade-point average to be certified for the minor.
Program name: Minor in Digital Media, Arts, and Technology

Requirements: For admission to the minor, students must be enrolled in a baccalaureate program and have completed at least 30 credits at Penn State or another accredited institution.
Program name: Minor in Earth Science and Policy

Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. In addition, at least six credits of the supplement must be at the 400 level. Entrance to Minor: Students can apply for admission to the minor after they have achieved at least fifth-semester standing.
Program name: Minor in Earth Systems

Requirements: A student may apply for the minor in the department or through the office of the minor adviser. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. To graduate with a minor in Asian Studies, students must have at least 18 credits in Asian Studies, with at least 6 credits at the 400 level.
Program name: Minor in East Asian Studies

Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor. At least six credits must be at the 400 level. Prescribed Courses: ECON 102 Introductory Microeconomic Analysis and Policy (3 credits), ECON 104 Introductory Macroeconomic Analysis and Policy (3 credits). Supporting Courses and Related Areas: Select 12 credits of ECON courses (excluding ECON 489, 495, 496) (12 credits).
Program name: Minor in Economics

Requirements: To graduate with a minor, students must satisfy the requirements for the minor, including at least 6 credits at the 400-level. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. A student must complete at least 18 credits of course work. At least 6 credits must be at the 400 level. In addition, the student must select at least 6 credits from a set of approved courses in Education Policy Studies and at least 6 credits from a set of approved courses in other related disciplines such as political science, sociology, or economics.
Program name: Minor in Education and Public Policy

Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be enrolled in a major that provides a sufficient background in mathematics and physics. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from any other degree or minor. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Program name: Minor in Electrical Engineering

Requirements: Students must apply for admission to the minor after they have earned at least 18 credits at Penn State and have been admitted to a major.
Program name: Minor in Energy and Sustainability Policy

Requirements: For admission to the minor, students must have completed at least 30 credits at Penn State with a minimum grade point average of 2.00. In addition, students must have completed ECON 102 GS(3) and MATH 110 GQ(4) or MATH 140 GQ(4) with a grade of C or better. A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor.
Program name: Minor in Energy Business and Finance

Requirements: A grade of C or better is required for all courses in the minor, as specified by Senate Policy 59-10. At least six credits of the minor must be unique from the prescribed courses required by a student's major(s). In addition, at least six credits of the minor must be taken at the 400-level.
Program name: Minor in English

Requirements: To be admitted to the minor, students must be enrolled in a baccalaureate program at the University.
